:::{#def-differentiable}
#### Differentiable function

A function $f$ is **differentiable at** $x = c$
[@wikipedia_differentiable_function]
if the limit (@def-limit) of the difference quotient (@def-difference-quotient) as $h \to 0$,

$$f'(c) \eqdef \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h},$$

exists and is finite.
The value of this limit is denoted $f'(c)$.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 2.1, p. 100]

:::
